questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Bahrain?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Culture” part of the Bahrain article.

questions.proof: Manama, Bahrain's capital city, is as modern as other cities in the world.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Bahrain?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Bahrain on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Modern history” part of the Bahrain article.

questions.proof: The modern history of Bahrain begins with Great Britain exploring the area, trying to keep Iran from taking more land.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Bahrain?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Culture” part of the Bahrain article.

questions.proof: Arabic is the official language, but many people speak English.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Saudi Arabia is to the west and is connected to Bahrain by the King Fahd Causeway, and _____ is to the south across the Persian Gulf.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Causeway”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Bahrain article.

questions.proof: Saudi Arabia is to the west and is connected to Bahrain by the King Fahd Causeway, and Qatar is to the south across the Persian Gulf.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “About 2300 BC, Bahrain started trading with Mesopotamia (now _____) and the Indus Valley (now near India).”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Mesopotamia”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Bahrain article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: About 2300 BC, Bahrain started trading with Mesopotamia (now Iraq) and the Indus Valley (now near India).
